text: Gustave "Gus" Fitzhugh Touchard Jr., also known as Gustav, was an American tennis player active in the early 20th century and reached a highest ranking of No. 4 in the United States. Born on January 11, 1888, in New York to Gustave and Margaret McPherson Touchard, he played his first tournament in 1907 at the New York Tennis Club Open, reaching the semi-finals. In 1908, he reached his first final at the New York Metropolitan Championships, where he lost to Ross Burchard. In 1909, he won four singles titles: the Amackassin Club Invitation against Frederick Clark Inman, the Harlem Tennis Club Invitation against Wylie Grant, the Bronx County Championships against Theodore Pell, and the New York Tennis Club Open against Theodore Pell; he also reached the final of the New England Championships that year. At the US Nationals, he partnered with Raymond D. Little to win the 1911 doubles title and reached the 1912 doubles final. At the Tri-State Championships in Cincinnati, he won the 1912 singles title over Richard H. Palmer and reached the singles final again in 1913, losing to William S. McEllroy. He won the U.S. National Indoor Tennis Championships three consecutive years—1913, 1914, and 1915—and claimed the singles title at the New Jersey State Championships in 1915. In 1912, he reached the final of the US Clay Court Championship, losing to Richard Norris Williams. On October 11, 1911, he married Emeline Williams Holmes, and the marriage produced at least one child, Emlen Holmes, born on May 24, 1914. In July 1915, he admitted to stealing 24 dozen golf balls from the sporting goods store where he was employed. After being rejected by the United States aviation corps, he joined the Royal Flying Corps Canada at Camp Borden and died in 1918 at Toronto General Hospital following a throat operation.
